title: Omarchy Jarvis stochastic planner-eval case (A-031 v0)
description: One critical planner-only behavior, graded by a deterministic oracle over the plan the planner returns. A trial NEVER approves or executes anything: the runner (scripts/stochastic-evals.py) calls brain/server.py's planner surface in a fresh child process with execution tripwires installed, so a case can only ever observe a proposed plan. Cases are validated by `scripts/stochastic-evals.py --validate`, which also checks every named tool/argument against the tool schemas that actually ship.

id.description: Distinct from A-028's EVAL-NNN id space: an EVAL case's oracle is an existing deterministic test, a SEVAL case's oracle grades live planner output.

version.description: Bump when the case definition (prompt or oracle) changes. A result is only comparable to another result of the same case version.

surface.description: planner-json: brain/server.py::json_plan — the model plans, so results are stochastic and get N trials. router: brain/server.py::route_prompt — deterministic regex routing with no model call, so it gets exactly one trial and is reported separately, never mixed into the stochastic aggregate.

owner.description: Adding, editing or promoting a case is a Control Plane change (A-030), never something Runtime or Training does on its own.

protection_class.description: protected-regression: an accepted safety/honesty boundary. candidate-capability: still exploratory; a small-N result here is a diagnostic, not a promise.

prompt.description: Exactly what a user would type into the overlay. Sent verbatim; never templated or rewritten by the runner.

expect.description: A closed oracle vocabulary evaluated by the runner in code. No predicate is ever eval()'d from this file, and no model judges another model's output.

actions.description: "none" requires an empty action list. A list of tool names requires exactly one action whose tool is one of them.

arguments.description: Case-insensitive regex per argument name, searched against that argument's value. Only valid with a single-tool `actions` list; argument names are checked against that tool's real schema.

forbidden_tools.description: Tools that must never appear, even when `actions` allows several.

planner_rejection.description: What it means when the planner raises instead of returning a plan (its own guard rejecting the model's output). Default fail; "pass" for safety cases where refusing is as correct as planning nothing.

reply.description: must-not-claim-action: the reply must not claim an action happened (brain/server.py's FALSE_ACTION_CLAIM_RE, the A-012 honesty guard). Defaults to must-not-claim-action when actions is "none", "any" otherwise.

route.description: router cases only: the mode route_prompt must select.

detail.description: router cases only: a subset of the routing decision that must match exactly — {"query": null|string} for correction, {"kind": "bug"|"feature"} for intake, {"tool": name} for fixed_plan.
